GitLab MCP Server

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

English 한국어 简体中文 Português (Brasil)

📖 Documentation → · llms.txt · llms-full.txt

 Default: 40 tools (38 core + discover tools + help ). 290 tools exist in total (287 in toolsets + execute graphql + discover tools + help ). Start lean; call discover tools to activate more for this session.

 Token budget: MCP clients send the whole tools/list to the model at session start. Keep the default ( 40 tools, 12k schema tokens). Call discover tools to activate a category for this session (session-only; with OAUTH STATELESS MODE=true persist a named GITLAB TOOLSETS list), or use Skill + CLI and skip MCP schemas. Do not set GITLAB TOOLSETS=all — it loads all tools and costs 73k schema tokens. See tools/list size and comparison.

Install the zereight-mcp-gitlab binary first with npm install -g @zereight/mcp-gitlab , or Homebrew brew tap zereight/gitlab-mcp and brew install zereight/gitlab-mcp/zereight-mcp-gitlab . Official MCP Registry listing: io.github.zereight/gitlab-mcp . One-liner: npx -y @zereight/mcp-gitlab@latest .

 Without → With

 Without this MCP With this MCP 
 ---------------- ------------- 
 Paste MR URLs and diffs into chat list merge request changed files → batched get merge request file diff 
 Hunt job logs in the GitLab UI get pipeline job output with pagination 
 Re-explain the project path every turn project id=group%2Fproject and merge request iid=123 

 Three install paths

 Path When How 
 ---- ---- --- 
 Local IDE Cursor, Claude Code, Codex on your machine stdio + PAT or local OAuth 
 Shared HTTP Team or hosted MCP Streamable HTTP URL + remote auth or MCP OAuth 
 Claude.ai Claude web connectors Public HTTPS + GITLAB MCP OAUTH

 Agent paste-prompt

Copy this into an agent that can edit MCP config:

 

 Remote HTTP

First-class option for a hosted or self-hosted server. Point the client at a Streamable HTTP URL:

 

- Hosted / Claude.ai: GITLAB MCP OAUTH=true on the server (see MCP OAuth)
- Per-user PAT headers: REMOTE AUTHORIZATION=true (see Remote Authorization)
- Local Docker examples are in Usage

 Skill + CLI (no MCP required)

Skill + CLI is an equal path, not a fallback. Same workflows, full payloads in a terminal, no MCP registration.

 

See CLI without MCP and skills/gitlab-mcp/ .

 MCP vs Human CLI

 Use MCP when Use the CLI when 
 ------------ ---------------- 
 The agent needs structured tools in chat You need the full payload (diffs, logs, artifacts) 
 jmespath or compact results are enough GITLAB MCP COMPACT RESULTS is on and you want the rest in a terminal 
 You already registered the server You have a PAT or ran auth and do not want MCP 

Human CLI is never compacted. Destructive tools and GITLAB TOOL POLICY APPROVE tools need --yes .

 Tips

 project id is a numeric ID or a URL-encoded path. Example: group group , project project , merge request !123 → project id=group%2Fproject , merge request iid=123 . Nested groups use %2F between every segment ( group%2Fsubgroup%2Fproject ).

 FAQ

 How do I authenticate? Local desktop: GITLAB PERSONAL ACCESS TOKEN (or GITLAB PERSONAL ACCESS TOKEN FILE ) is the simplest. Local OAuth is GITLAB USE OAUTH=true . Remote Claude.ai uses GITLAB MCP OAUTH . Multi-user HTTP uses REMOTE AUTHORIZATION and a per-request token header.

 Why do I only see 40 tools? The default core toolset is 38 tools plus always-on discover tools and help . That is intentional: a client sends every listed schema to the model up front. Call discover tools with no args to list categories, then pass a category ( pipelines , wiki , …) to activate it for this session. Session-only; with OAUTH STATELESS MODE=true persist a named GITLAB TOOLSETS list. Do not set GITLAB TOOLSETS=all — it loads all schemas ( 73k tokens) and still does not enable api .

 Local OAuth vs MCP OAuth vs remote auth? Local OAuth opens a browser on the same machine as the server. MCP OAuth is for a public HTTPS server and clients such as Claude.ai. Remote authorization forwards the caller's PAT or job token; there is no OAuth dance.

 How do I shrink huge replies? Pass jmespath on any tool call. Or set GITLAB MCP COMPACT RESULTS=true so oversized MCP replies become a preview plus a CLI command. Use the CLI when you need the full payload.

 Why is the api toolset dangerous? gitlab api request bypasses group/project allowlists, other tool filters, and per-tool safety checks. Prompt injection can drive it. Enable it only by listing api in GITLAB TOOLSETS . all , discover tools , and GITLAB TOOLS do not.

 Cursor rule / CLAUDE.md snippet

 

 

 @zereight/mcp-gitlab

 Agent-workflow-optimized GitLab MCP — manage projects, merge requests, issues, pipelines, wiki, releases, tags, milestones, and more through stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP.

Supports PAT, OAuth, read-only mode, dynamic API URLs, and remote authorization for VS Code, Claude, Cursor, Copilot, and other MCP clients.

 Why use this GitLab MCP?

- Default 40 tools (38 core + discover tools + help ); 290 total — start lean; call discover tools to activate more without CQRS-style grouping. GITLAB TOOLSETS=all loads all schemas ( 73k tokens); prefer discover-on-demand or Skill + CLI
- MR 2-step review — list merge request changed files → batched get merge request file diff 
- Agent Skill built in — workflow guidance in skills/gitlab-mcp/ 
- Flexible auth — Personal Access Token, local OAuth2 browser flow, MCP OAuth proxy, and per-request remote authorization
- Multiple transports — stdio for local clients, SSE for legacy clients, and Streamable HTTP for modern remote deployments
- Client-friendly setup — examples for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Copilot, Cline, Roo Code, Cursor, Kilo Code, a

install.title: Install
install.html:
Install the binary first (npm install -g @zereight/mcp-gitlab, or Homebrew brew tap zereight/gitlab-mcp https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp then brew install zereight/gitlab-mcp/zereight-mcp-gitlab). Read the token without echo:

read -rs GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN && export GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

# Claude Code
claude mcp add gitlab --transport stdio --scope local --env GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN="$GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN" --env GITLAB_API_URL=https://gitlab.com/api/v4 -- zereight-mcp-gitlab

# Codex
codex mcp add gitlab --env GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN="$GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN" --env GITLAB_API_URL=https://gitlab.com/api/v4 -- zereight-mcp-gitlab

Other clients: VS Code · GitHub Copilot · JSON clients · Cursor details

usage.title: Usage
usage.html:
Setup Overview
Authentication Methods

The server supports four authentication methods:

For local/desktop use (most common):

  1. Personal Access Token (GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN or GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE) — simplest setup
  2. OAuth2 — Local Browser (GITLAB_USE_OAUTH) — recommended for better security

For server/remote deployments:

  1. OAuth2 — MCP Proxy (GITLAB_MCP_OAUTH) — for remote MCP clients such as Claude.ai
  2. Remote Authorization (REMOTE_AUTHORIZATION) — multi-user deployments where each caller provides their own token
Quick setup paths
  • Claude Code: see Claude Code Setup Guide
  • VS Code: see VS Code Setup Guide
  • GitHub Copilot: see GitHub Copilot Setup Guide
  • Codex: see Codex Setup Guide
  • Cursor: see Cursor Setup Guide
  • Factory AI Droid / OpenClaw / OpenCode style clients: see JSON-Based MCP Clients Setup Guide
  • OAuth browser flow details: see OAuth2 Authentication Setup Guide
  • OAuth without a localhost callback (SSO, remote shell, background clients): run zereight-mcp-gitlab auth (GitLab 17.9+ device flow; 17.2–17.8 need oauth2_device_grant_flow), then start the server with GITLAB_USE_OAUTH=true. See standalone device-flow command.

For the simplest local setup, start with a Personal Access Token. For browser-based local auth, use OAuth2. For remote or multi-user deployments, continue to the MCP OAuth and Remote Authorization sections later in this README.

Install the server once:

brew tap zereight/gitlab-mcp https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp
brew install zereight/gitlab-mcp/zereight-mcp-gitlab

Or with npm:

npm install -g @zereight/mcp-gitlab

Or with Nix, by adding this flake to your own:

# flake.nix
inputs.gitlab-mcp.url = "github:zereight/gitlab-mcp";

# wherever you configure your MCP client:
command = lib.getExe inputs.gitlab-mcp.packages.${system}.default;

The store path is pinned by your lock file; update it with nix flake update gitlab-mcp.

The examples use zereight-mcp-gitlab, a less collision-prone alias for the legacy mcp-gitlab binary. If your MCP client cannot find it, use the absolute path from which zereight-mcp-gitlab.

No global install? Pin npx to the previous stable release (the version these docs recommend), for example npx -y @zereight/mcp-gitlab@2.3.30. If you set GITLAB_MASKING_ENABLED, use 2.3.29 or later (or @latest): older releases return the values of CI/CD variables that GitLab flags masked or hidden in plain text. If you always want the newest release, use npx -y @zereight/mcp-gitlab@latest instead. To try a fix merged to main before the next stable release, use npx -y @zereight/mcp-gitlab@next, a pre-release build that is not meant for production. The server prints a notice to stderr on startup when a newer version is available (disable with GITLAB_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=true).

Claude Desktop one-click install (MCP Bundle)

Every GitHub release after v2.3.1 ships a gitlab-mcp.mcpb MCP Bundle. Download the latest bundle and open it with Claude Desktop (or drag it into Settings → Extensions). Claude Desktop asks for your Personal Access Token (stored as a sensitive value) and lets you set GITLAB_API_URL, GITLAB_PERMISSION_MODE, GITLAB_TOOLSETS, and GITLAB_MASKING_ENABLED. No separate Node.js or npm install is needed.

To build the bundle from source, run npm run pack:mcpb (writes gitlab-mcp.mcpb).

Using CLI Arguments (for clients with env var issues)

Some MCP clients (like GitHub Copilot CLI) have issues with environment variables. Use CLI arguments instead:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gitlab": {
      "command": "zereight-mcp-gitlab",
      "args": ["--token=YOUR_GITLAB_TOKEN", "--api-url=https://gitlab.com/api/v4"],
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}

Available CLI arguments:

  • --token - GitLab Personal Access Token (replaces GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN)
  • --api-url - GitLab API URL (replaces GITLAB_API_URL)
  • --read-only=true - Deprecated (removed in next major (v3.0.0)); use --permission-mode=readonly instead (replaces GITLAB_READ_ONLY_MODE)
  • --permission-mode - Permission level: readonly, modify (no delete or teardown tools), or full (replaces GITLAB_PERMISSION_MODE, default full)
  • --toolsets - Named toolsets (replaces GITLAB_TOOLSETS; unset uses the lean core default). Do not pass all unless you accept ~73k schema tokens. gitlab_api_request needs --toolsets=api
  • --tools=list_issues - Add individual tools (replaces GITLAB_TOOLS)
  • --use-wiki=true - Deprecated (removed in next major (v3.0.0)); use --toolsets=core,wiki instead (replaces USE_GITLAB_WIKI)
  • --use-milestone=true - Deprecated (removed in next major (v3.0.0)); use --toolsets=core,milestones instead (replaces USE_MILESTONE)
  • --use-pipeline=true - Deprecated (removed in next major (v3.0.0)); use --toolsets=core,pipelines and append validate_ci_lint,validate_project_ci_lint to the existing --tools list (or set --tools=validate_ci_lint,validate_project_ci_lint when that list is unset) (replaces USE_PIPELINE)
  • --disable-version-check=true - Disable the startup new-version notice (replaces GITLAB_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK)
  • --masking-enabled=true - Enable text-response masking (replaces GITLAB_MASKING_ENABLED)
  • --masking-config - Path to a masking configuration file (replaces GITLAB_MASKING_CONFIG)
  • --masking-policy-file - Path to a protected managed-policy file (replaces GITLAB_MASKING_POLICY_FILE)
  • --masking-workspace-dir - Directory used to resolve masking files (replaces GITLAB_MASKING_WORKSPACE_DIR)
  • --download-dir - Directory download_attachment and download_job_artifacts save files under (replaces GITLAB_DOWNLOAD_DIR; default .gitlab-mcp-downloads)
  • --compact-results=true - Truncate oversized MCP tool replies and attach a CLI command for the full payload (replaces GITLAB_MCP_COMPACT_RESULTS; default off)
  • --compact-result-chars - Character threshold for compacting (replaces GITLAB_MCP_COMPACT_RESULT_CHARS; default 4000)
  • --compact-tools - Comma-separated tool names to compact when oversized, without turning global compact on (replaces GITLAB_MCP_COMPACT_TOOLS)
  • --list-summary-default=true - list_* tools and mr_discussions treat an omitted summary argument as true; summary: false still returns the full JSON (replaces GITLAB_MCP_LIST_SUMMARY_DEFAULT; default off)
  • --audit-log=true - Opt-in NDJSON audit log of MCP tool calls for SIEM ingestion (replaces GITLAB_AUDIT_LOG; default off)
  • --audit-log-file - Append audit lines to this file; unset writes NDJSON to stderr, never stdout (replaces GITLAB_AUDIT_LOG_FILE)
  • --tool-profile - full (default) or slim. slim drops draft notes, emoji reactions, labels, CI catalog tools, and create_group from the initial list. Ignored when GITLAB_TOOLSETS is set (replaces GITLAB_TOOL_PROFILE)

If you already set GITLAB_TOOLSETS or --toolsets, append wiki, milestones, or pipelines to that list instead of replacing it. If you already set GITLAB_TOOLS or --tools, append validate_ci_lint and validate_project_ci_lint to that list instead of replacing it. An explicit list replaces the default core toolset; it does not merge.

CLI arguments take precedence over environment variables.

zereight-mcp-gitlab auth is a subcommand (not an MCP server flag). It runs GitLab device flow and exits. See CLI Arguments.
